trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria: Inclusion Criteria: - Type 2 diabetes - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease - HbA1c: 7.0% or above - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s) Exclusion Criteria: - Type 1 diabetes - Use of a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist (exenatide, liraglutide or other) or pramlintide or any dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitor within the 3 months prior to screening (trial start) - Use of insulin other than human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin within 3 months prior to screening. Short-term use of other insulin during this period in connection with intercurrent illness is allowed, at Investigator's discretion
trialMetadata.enrichedCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
  - >50% stenosis of coronary, carotid, or lower extremity arteries
  - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease
  - Ankle-brachial index <0.9
  - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Anti-diabetic drug naïve or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Asymptomatic cardiac ischemia documented by positive nuclear imaging test, exercise test or dobutamine stress echo
  - Chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III
  - Chronic renal failure:
  - Glycated hemoglobin ≥7.0%
  - HbA1c: 7.0% or above
  - History of symptomatic CHD documented by positive exercise stress test or any cardiac imaging or unstable angina with ECG changes
  - Hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG or imaging
  - Left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction by imaging
  - Microalbuminuria or proteinuria
  - No Prior cardiovascular disease group: Age ≥60 y and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior MI
  - Prior cardiovascular disease cohort: age ≥50 and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior coronary, carotid or peripheral arterial revascularization
  - Prior stroke or TIA
  - Type 2 diabetes
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - Acute coronary or cerebrovascular event in the previous 14 days
  - Acute decompensation of glycemic control
  - Calcitonin ≥50 ng/L
  - Chronic heart failure (NYHA class IV)
  - Current continuous renal replacement therapy
  - Currently planned coronary, carotid, or peripheral artery revascularization
  - End-stage liver disease
  - Family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - History of solid organ transplant or awaiting solid organ transplant
  - Malignant neoplasm
  - Personal history of non-familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - Type 1 diabetes
  - Use of a GLP-1 receptor agonist (exenatide, liraglutide or other) or pramlintide or any DPP-4 inhibitor within the 3 months prior to screening
  - Use of insulin other than human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin within 3 months prior to screening. Short-term use of other insulin during this period in connection with intercurrent illness is allowed, at Investigator’s discretion

trialMetadata.enrichedCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
  - >50% stenosis of coronary, carotid, or lower extremity arteries
  - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease
  - Ankle-brachial index <0.9
  - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Anti-diabetic drug naïve or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Asymptomatic cardiac ischemia documented by positive nuclear imaging test, exercise test or dobutamine stress echo
  - Chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III
  - Chronic renal failure:
  - Glycated hemoglobin ≥7.0%
  - HbA1c: 7.0% or above
  - History of symptomatic CHD documented by positive exercise stress test or any cardiac imaging or unstable angina with ECG changes
  - Hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG or imaging
  - Left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction by imaging
  - Microalbuminuria or proteinuria
  - No Prior cardiovascular disease group: Age ≥60 y and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior MI
  - Prior cardiovascular disease cohort: age ≥50 and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior coronary, carotid or peripheral arterial revascularization
  - Prior stroke or TIA
  - Type 2 diabetes
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - Acute coronary or cerebrovascular event in the previous 14 days
  - Acute decompensation of glycemic control
  - Calcitonin ≥50 ng/L
  - Chronic heart failure (NYHA class IV)
  - Current continuous renal replacement therapy
  - Currently planned coronary, carotid, or peripheral artery revascularization
  - End-stage liver disease
  - Family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - History of solid organ transplant or awaiting solid organ transplant
  - Malignant neoplasm
  - Personal history of non-familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - Type 1 diabetes
  - Use of a GLP-1 receptor agonist (exenatide, liraglutide or other) or pramlintide or any DPP-4 inhibitor within the 3 months prior to screening
  - Use of insulin other than human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin within 3 months prior to screening. Short-term use of other insulin during this period in connection with intercurrent illness is allowed, at Investigator’s discretion

  - >50% stenosis of coronary, carotid, or lower extremity arteries

  - Ankle-brachial index <0.9

  - Asymptomatic cardiac ischemia documented by positive nuclear imaging test, exercise test or dobutamine stress echo
  - Chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III
  - Chronic renal failure:
  - Glycated hemoglobin ≥7.0%
  - HbA1c: 7.0% or above
  - History of symptomatic CHD documented by positive exercise stress test or any cardiac imaging or unstable angina with ECG changes
  - Hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG or imaging
  - Left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction by imaging
  - Microalbuminuria or proteinuria
  - No Prior cardiovascular disease group: Age ≥60 y and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior MI

  - Prior coronary, carotid or peripheral arterial revascularization
  - Prior stroke or TIA
  - Type 2 diabetes
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - Acute coronary or cerebrovascular event in the previous 14 days
  - Acute decompensation of glycemic control
  - Calcitonin ≥50 ng/L
  - Chronic heart failure (NYHA class IV)
  - Current continuous renal replacement therapy
  - Currently planned coronary, carotid, or peripheral artery revascularization

  - Family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - History of solid organ transplant or awaiting solid organ transplant
  - Malignant neoplasm

  - Type 1 diabetes

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus prior to informed consent
2. Male or female patients on diet and exercise regimen who are drug naive or pre treated with any background therapy. Antidiabetic therapy has to be unchanged for 12 weeks prior to randomization.
3. Glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) of \>= 7.0% and \<=10% for patients on background therapy or HbA1c \>= 7.0% and \<= 9.0% for drug naive patients
4. Age \>= 18 years
5. Body Mass index \<= 45 at Visit 1
6. Signed and dated informed consent
7. High cardiovascular risk

Exclusion criteria:

1. Uncontrolled hyperglycaemia with a glucose level \>240 mg/dl (\>13.3 mmol/L) after an overnight fast during placebo run-in and confirmed by a second measurement (not on the same day)
2. Indication of liver disease, defined by serum levels of either alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase ALT or alkaline phosphatase above 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN) as determined at screening and/or run in.
3. Planned cardiac surgery or angioplasty within 3 months
4. Impaired renal function, defined as Glomerular Filtration Rate \<30 ml/min (severe renal impairment, Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula) during screening or run in.
5. Bariatric surgery within the past two years and other gastrointestinal surgeries that induce chronic malabsorption
6. Blood dyscrasias or any disorders causing haemolysis or unstable Red Blood Cell (e.g. malaria, babesiosis, haemolytic anemia)
7. Medical history of cancer (except for basal cell carcinoma) and/or treatment for cancer within the last 5 years
8. Contraindications to background therapy according to the local label
9. Treatment with anti-obesity drugs (e.g. sibutramine, orlistat) 3 months prior to informed consent or any other treatment at the time of screening (i.e. surgery, aggressive diet regimen, etc.) leading to unstable body weight
10. Current treatment with systemic steroids at time of informed consent or change in dosage of thyroid hormones within 6 weeks prior to informed consent or any other uncontrolled endocrine disorder except type 2 diabetes mellitus
11. Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation \<+ 1 year prior to informed consent) who:

    * are nursing or pregnant or
    * are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control, or do not plan to continue using this method throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial. Acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems, oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence, double barrier method and vasectomised partner
12. Alcohol or drug abuse within the 3 months prior to informed consent that would interfere with trial participation or any ongoing condition leading to a decreased compliance to study procedures or study drug intake
13. Participation in another trial with an investigational drug within 30 days prior to informed consent
14. Any other clinical condition that would jeopardize patients safety while participating in this clinical trial
15. Acute coronary syndrome, stroke or TIA within 2 months prior to informed consent

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Documented diagnosis of T2DM before visit 1(screening).
2. Male or female patients who are drug-naïve or pre-treated with any antidiabetic background medication, excluding treatment with Glucagon-like Peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, Dipeptidyl-peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitors or Sodium Glucose Linked Transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors if =\> consecutive 7 days.
3. Stable antidiabetic background medication (unchanged daily dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to randomization. If insulin is part of the background therapy, the average daily insulin dose should not have changed by more than 10% within the 8 weeks prior to randomization compared with the daily insulin dose at randomization.
4. HbA1c of =\> 6.5% and \<= 10.0% at Visit 1 (screening)
5. Age =\> 18 years at Visit 1(screening). For Japan only: Age =\> 20 years at Visit 1
6. Body Mass Index (BMI) \<= 45 kg/m2 at Visit 1 (screening)
7. Signed and dated written informed consent by date of Visit 1(screening) in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation prior to any study related procedure
8. High risk of cardiovascular (CV) events defined by: 1) albuminuria (micro or macro) and previous macrovascular disease and/or 2) impaired renal function with predefined Urine Albumin Creatinine Ratio (UACR)

Exclusion criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Treatment (=\> 7 consecutive days) with GLP-1 receptor agonists, other DPP-4 inhibitors or SGLT-2 inhibitors prior to informed consent. Note: This also includes clinical trials where these antidiabetic drugs have been provided to the patient.
3. Active liver disease or impaired hepatic function, defined by serum levels of either Alanine Transaminase (ALT) (SGPT), Aspartate transaminase (AST) (SGOT), or alkaline phosphatase (AP) =\> 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN) as determined at Visit 1.
4. Estimated Glomerular filtration Rate (eGFR) \<15 ml/min/1.73 m2 (severe renal impairment or End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) formula), as determined during screening at Visit 1 and/or the need for maintenance dialysis.
5. Any previous (or planned within next 12 months) bariatric surgery (open or laparoscopic) or intervention (gastric sleeve).
6. Pre-planned coronary artery re-vascularisation (PCI, CABG) or any previous PCI and/or CABG \<= 2 months prior informed consent.
7. Known hypersensitivity or allergy to the investigational products or its excipients.
8. Any previous or current alcohol or drug abuse that would interfere with trial participation in the opinion of the investigator.
9. Participation in another trial with an investigational drug ongoing or within 2 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
10. Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation = 1 year prior to informed consent) who are nursing or pregnant, are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control (acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems (IUDs/IUSs), oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence (if allowed by local authorities), double barrier method and vasectomised partner) or do not plan to continue using acceptable method of birth control throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial.
11. Patients considered unreliable by the investigator concerning the requirements for follow up during the study and/or compliance with study drug administration, have a life expectancy less than 5 years for non-CV causes, or have cancer other than non-melanoma skin cancer within last 3 years, or has any other condition than mentioned which in the opinion of the investigator, would not allow safe participation in the study.
12. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS), diagnosed \<= 2 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
13. Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) \<= 3 months prior to visit 1 (screening).

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Type 2 diabetes
2. Elevated glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c): 6.5 - 8.5%, inclusive, if treatment naïve or mono-/dual therapy with metformin and/or an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor; 6.5 - 7.5%, inclusive, if treatment with sulphonylurea/glinide in mono- or dual (with metformin OR an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) therapy)
3. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease OR specified diabetes end-organ damage OR age =\> 70 years OR two or more specified cardiovascular risk factor
4. BMI =\< 45kg/m²
5. age between \>= 40 and =\< 85 years
6. signed and dated written International Conference of Harmonisation( ICF)
7. stable anti-diabetic background for at least 8 wks before study start

Exclusion criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes
2. Treatment with other antidiabetic drugs (e.g. rosiglitazone, pioglitazone, Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) analogue/agonists, Dipeptidyl-peptidase IV (DPP-IV) inhibitors or any insulin) prior to informed consent (previous short term use of insulin (up to two weeks) is allowed if taken at least 8 weeks prior informed consent)
3. treatment with any anti-obesity drug less than 3 months before ICF
4. uncontrolled hyperglycemia
5. previous or planned bariatric surgery or intervention
6. current or planned system corticoid treatment
7. change in thyroid hormones treatment
8. acute liver disease or impaired hepatic function
9. pre-planned coronary artery revascularization within 6 months of ICF
10. known hypersensitivity to any of the components
11. Inappropriateness of glimepiride treatment for renal safety issues according to local prescribing information
12. congestive heart failure class III or IV
13. acute or chronic metabolic acidosis
14. hereditary galactose intolerance
15. alcohol or drug abuse
16. participation in another trail with IMP given 2 months before Investigational Medicinal/Medical Product (IMP) start
17. pre-menopausal women who are nursing or pregnant or of child-bearing potential and not willing to use acceptable method of birth control
18. patients considered reliable by the investigator
19. acute coronary syndrome =\< 6 wks before ICF
20. stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) =\< 3 months prior to ICF

A Comparison of Ticagrelor (AZD6140) and Clopidogrel in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome

1. Clinical Question

Population: Patients eligible for ticagrelor treatment for acute coronary syndromes (ACS).

Intervention: Initiation of ticagrelor at index date.

Comparator: Non-initiation of ticagrelor among eligible patients (target minus treated).

Outcome: Death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke.

Estimand: Intention-to-treat (ITT) analogue.

Emulation Scope: Short-horizon emulation, not full replication.

2. Target Trial Specification

Component Original Trial Emulation Mismatch Risk
Eligibility Hospitalized for chest pain and potential ACS Eligible for ticagrelor treatment for ACS Moderate
Treatment strategy Initiation of ticagrelor Initiation of ticagrelor at index date Moderate
Time zero Randomization date Date of first eligible ticagrelor prescription for treated patients; corresponding index date assignment for comparator patients Moderate
Outcome Death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke Primary Outcome Moderate
Follow-up 365 days 30 days High
Causal contrast ITT ITT analogue Moderate
Confounding control Randomization IPTW (PSM fallback) High

3. Data Source & Cohort Construction

Data provenance: Unknown (major limitation).

Cohort sizes: Treatment N = 191, Comparator N = 918.

Treatment definition: Initiation of ticagrelor at index date.

Comparator definition: Non-initiation of ticagrelor among eligible patients.

Eligibility criteria summary: Patients eligible for ticagrelor treatment for ACS.

Time parameters: Washout period = 180 days, Grace period = 30 days, Follow-up duration = 30 days.

4. Confounding Control & Diagnostics

Analysis method: IPTW (PSM fallback).

Balance diagnostics: 9 covariates were checked.

Max |SMD| after weighting: 1.3582.

Propensity score weighting did NOT achieve adequate covariate balance. The reported effect estimate is highly vulnerable to residual confounding.

Imbalanced covariates (|SMD| > 0.1): age, Cond: Coronary arteriosclerosis, Cond: Peripheral vascular disease, Cond: Myocardial infarction.

Limitations: Measured confounders poorly controlled; unmeasured confounding remains.

5. Results

Total outcome events: 149 (treatment: 18, comparator: 131).

Hazard Ratio: 0.7503, 95% CI: 0.5523-1.0195, p-value: 0.0663.

The result is not statistically significant, and the estimate is imprecise.

6. Comparison with Original Trial

  • Follow-up duration: Original: 365 days, Emulation: 30 days.
  • Enrollment: Original: 18624, Emulation: 1109.
  • Outcome events: Not specified for original trial.
  • Hazard Ratio: Not specified for original trial.

This emulation differs materially from the original trial in follow-up duration, enrollment, and treatment definition.

7. Limitations

  • Short follow-up (30 days < 365 days).
  • Unmeasured confounding (IPTW/PSM controls only measured confounders).
  • MEASURED confounding poorly controlled: max |SMD| = 1.36 after weighting.
  • Causal interpretation not supported — identification assumptions not verified.
  • Data source 'Unknown': major provenance limitation.
  • Residual covariate imbalance: age, Cond: Coronary arteriosclerosis, Cond: Peripheral vascular disease, Cond: Myocardial infarction.

8. Interpretation & Next Steps

  • Operational feasibility: Yes
  • Effect estimation reliability: Poor
  • Clinical interpretability: Not supported
  • Causal interpretability: Not supported

Recommend next analyses: longer follow-up, sensitivity analyses, and improved confounding control.

This analysis is a pipeline feasibility study and exploratory in nature; it is not causal evidence or a clinical recommendation.

reasoning.method: PSM is selected because it is well-suited for scenarios where the treatment cohort is modest and the comparator-to-treatment size ratio is reasonably balanced. With a comparator ratio of 0.5x, PSM can effectively retain pairs, making it a strong choice for this analysis.

strategy.diagnosisSummary: Review treatment/comparator size, relative pool balance, and follow-up length before choosing the adjustment method.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: IPTW is less suitable here because the comparator advantage is limited, reducing the benefit of weighting. Although the treatment cohort is large, the smaller comparator pool does not support the stable weights needed for IPTW to be most effective.

Stratification is a more conservative fallback option and is less favored than matching or weighting in this workflow. While both cohorts are large enough for multi-stratum comparisons, PSM offers a more robust adjustment in this context.

Mahalanobis matching is best reserved for situations where covariate geometry is crucial, which is not the case here. The current cohort sizes do not justify preferring Mahalanobis over simpler methods like PSM.

liraglutide vs placebo for Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke

Generated: 2026-04-22T08:42:53.611122Z NCT: NCT01179048 Data source: Unknown Method: IPTW (PSM fallback)

Liraglutide Effect and Action in Diabetes: Evaluation of Cardiovascular Outcome Results

1. Clinical Question

Population: Patients with type 2 diabetes and specified cardiovascular risk factors.

Intervention: Initiation of liraglutide.

Comparator: Non-initiation of liraglutide among eligible patients (target minus treated).

Outcome: Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke.

Estimand: Intention-to-treat (ITT) analogue.

Emulation Scope: Short-horizon emulation, not full replication.

2. Target Trial Specification

Component Original Trial Emulation Mismatch Risk
Eligibility Type 2 diabetes, age ≥50 with cardiovascular conditions Type 2 diabetes, age ≥50 with cardiovascular conditions Moderate
Treatment strategy Liraglutide Initiation of liraglutide at index date Moderate
Time zero Randomization date Date of first eligible liraglutide prescription for treated patients; corresponding index date assignment for comparator patients Moderate
Outcome Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke Primary Outcome Moderate
Follow-up 365 days 30 days High
Causal contrast Liraglutide vs placebo Initiation vs non-initiation of liraglutide Moderate
Confounding control Randomization IPTW (PSM fallback) High

3. Data Source & Cohort Construction

Major Limitation: Data source is Unknown.

Cohort sizes: Treatment N = 1150, Comparator N = 581.

Treatment definition: Initiation of liraglutide at index date.

Comparator definition: Non-initiation of liraglutide among eligible patients.

Eligibility criteria: Type 2 diabetes, age ≥50 with cardiovascular conditions.

Time parameters: Washout period = 180 days, Grace period = 30 days, Follow-up duration = 30 days.

4. Confounding Control & Diagnostics

Analysis method: IPTW (PSM fallback).

Balance diagnostics: 17 covariates checked.

Max |SMD| after weighting: 1.6049.

Critical: Propensity score weighting did NOT achieve adequate covariate balance. The reported effect estimate is highly vulnerable to residual confounding.

Imbalanced covariates (|SMD| > 0.1): age, race_concept_id, Cond: Acute myocardial infarction, Cond: Congestive rheumatic heart failure, Cond: Atherosclerosis of arteries of the extremities, Cond: Hypertensive disorder, Cond: Cerebral artery occlusion, Cond: Carotid artery stenosis, Cond: Chronic kidney disease stage 4, Cond: Left ventricular hypertrophy, Cond: Microalbuminuria, Cond: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, Proc: Arterial bypass graft, Proc: Fluoroscopy guided percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of carotid artery with contrast, Proc: Angiectomy with anastomosis of lower limb artery.

Limitations: Measured confounders controlled, but unmeasured confounding remains.

5. Results

Total outcome events: 296 (treatment: 182, comparator: 114).

Hazard Ratio: 0.816, 95% CI: 0.663-1.004, p-value: 0.055.

Statistical significance: Not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.05).

Conclusion: Estimate is imprecise.

6. Comparison with Original Trial

  • Follow-up duration: Original trial = 365 days, Emulation = 30 days.
  • Enrollment: Original trial = 9341, Emulation = 1731.
  • Outcome events: Not specified for original trial.
  • Hazard Ratio: Not specified for original trial.

This emulation differs materially from the original trial in follow-up duration, enrollment, and treatment definition. Concordance assessment must be qualified by the mismatch analysis.

7. Limitations

  • Short follow-up (30 days < 365 days).
  • Unmeasured confounding (IPTW/PSM controls only measured confounders).
  • MEASURED confounding poorly controlled: max |SMD| = 1.60 after weighting.
  • Causal interpretation not supported — identification assumptions not verified.
  • Data source 'Unknown': major provenance limitation.
  • Residual covariate imbalance: age, race_concept_id, Cond: Acute myocardial infarction, Cond: Congestive rheumatic heart failure, Cond: Atherosclerosis of arteries of the extremities, Cond: Hypertensive disorder, Cond: Cerebral artery occlusion, Cond: Carotid artery stenosis, Cond: Chronic kidney disease stage 4, Cond: Left ventricular hypertrophy, Cond: Microalbuminuria, Cond: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, Proc: Arterial bypass graft, Proc: Fluoroscopy guided percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of carotid artery with contrast, Proc: Angiectomy with anastomosis of lower limb artery.

8. Interpretation & Next Steps

  • Operational feasibility: Yes
  • Effect estimation reliability: Poor
  • Clinical interpretability: Not supported
  • Causal interpretability: Not supported

Recommend next analyses: longer follow-up, sensitivity analyses, and improved confounding control.

Final statement: This analysis is an exploratory pipeline feasibility and is NOT causal evidence or a clinical recommendation.

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria: Inclusion Criteria: - Type 2 diabetes - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease - HbA1c: 7.0% or above - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s) Exclusion Criteria: - Type 1 diabetes - Use of a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist (exenatide, liraglutide or other) or pramlintide or any dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitor within the 3 months prior to screening (trial start) - Use of insulin other than human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin within 3 months prior to screening. Short-term use of other insulin during this period in connection with intercurrent illness is allowed, at Investigator's discretion
trialMetadata.enrichedCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
  - >50% stenosis of coronary, carotid, or lower extremity arteries
  - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease
  - Ankle-brachial index <0.9
  - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Anti-diabetic drug naïve or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Asymptomatic cardiac ischemia documented by positive nuclear imaging test, exercise test or dobutamine stress echo
  - Chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III
  - Chronic renal failure:
  - Glycated hemoglobin ≥7.0%
  - HbA1c: 7.0% or above
  - History of symptomatic CHD documented by positive exercise stress test or any cardiac imaging or unstable angina with ECG changes
  - Hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG or imaging
  - Left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction by imaging
  - Microalbuminuria or proteinuria
  - No Prior cardiovascular disease group: Age ≥60 y and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior MI
  - Prior cardiovascular disease cohort: age ≥50 and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior coronary, carotid or peripheral arterial revascularization
  - Prior stroke or TIA
  - Type 2 diabetes
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - Acute coronary or cerebrovascular event in the previous 14 days
  - Acute decompensation of glycemic control
  - Calcitonin ≥50 ng/L
  - Chronic heart failure (NYHA class IV)
  - Current continuous renal replacement therapy
  - Currently planned coronary, carotid, or peripheral artery revascularization
  - End-stage liver disease
  - Family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - History of solid organ transplant or awaiting solid organ transplant
  - Malignant neoplasm

rejectedAlternatives.reason: IPTW is less suitable here because the comparator advantage is limited, reducing the benefit of weighting despite the larger treatment cohort.

payload.reportHtml:
liraglutide vs placebo for Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke

Generated: 2026-04-22T12:22:06.550925Z NCT: NCT01179048 Data source: Unknown Method: IPTW (PSM fallback)

Liraglutide Effect and Action in Diabetes: Evaluation of Cardiovascular Outcome Results

1. Clinical Question

Population: Patients with type 2 diabetes and specified cardiovascular risk factors.

Intervention: Initiation of liraglutide.

Comparator: Non-initiation of liraglutide among eligible patients (target minus treated).

Outcome: Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke.

Estimand: Intention-to-treat (ITT) analogue.

Emulation Scope: Short-horizon emulation, not full replication.

2. Target Trial Specification

Component Original Trial Emulation Mismatch Risk
Eligibility Type 2 diabetes, age ≥50 with cardiovascular risk Type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk factors Moderate
Treatment strategy Liraglutide initiation Initiation of liraglutide at index date Moderate
Time zero Randomization date Date of first eligible liraglutide prescription for treated patients; corresponding index date assignment for comparator patients Moderate
Outcome Cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke Primary Outcome Moderate
Follow-up 365 days 30 days High
Causal contrast Liraglutide vs placebo Target minus treated Moderate
Confounding control Randomization IPTW (PSM fallback) High

3. Data Source & Cohort Construction

Major Limitation: Data source is 'Unknown'.

Cohort Sizes: Treatment N = 1150, Comparator N = 581.

Treatment Definition: Initiation of liraglutide at index date.

Comparator Definition: Non-initiation of liraglutide among eligible patients.

Eligibility Criteria Summary: Type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular risk factors.

Time Parameters: Washout period = 180 days, Grace period = 30 days, Follow-up duration = 30 days.

4. Confounding Control & Diagnostics

Analysis Method: IPTW was used; PSM fallback not applied.

Balance Diagnostics: 17 covariates checked.

Max |SMD| after weighting: 1.6049.

Critical Issue: Propensity score weighting did NOT achieve adequate covariate balance. The reported effect estimate is highly vulnerable to residual confounding.

Imbalanced Covariates (|SMD| > 0.1): age, race_concept_id, Cond: Acute myocardial infarction, Cond: Congestive rheumatic heart failure, Cond: Atherosclerosis of arteries of the extremities, Cond: Hypertensive disorder, Cond: Cerebral artery occlusion, Cond: Carotid artery stenosis, Cond: Chronic kidney disease stage 4, Cond: Left ventricular hypertrophy, Cond: Microalbuminuria, Cond: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, Proc: Arterial bypass graft, Proc: Fluoroscopy guided percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of carotid artery with contrast, Proc: Angiectomy with anastomosis of lower limb artery.

Limitations: Unmeasured confounding remains.

5. Results

Total Outcome Events: 296 (Treatment: 182, Comparator: 114).

Hazard Ratio: 0.816, 95% CI: 0.663-1.004, p-value: 0.055.

Statistical Significance: Not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.05).

Conclusion: Estimate is imprecise.

6. Comparison with Original Trial

  • Follow-up Duration: Emulation: 30 days; Original Trial: 365 days.
  • Enrollment: Emulation: 1731; Original Trial: 9341.
  • Outcome Events: Emulation: 296; Original Trial: Not specified.
  • Hazard Ratio: Emulation: 0.816; Original Trial: Not specified.

This emulation differs materially from the original trial in follow-up duration, enrollment, and treatment definition.

7. Limitations

  • Short follow-up (30 days < 365 days).
  • Unmeasured confounding (IPTW/PSM controls only measured confounders).
  • MEASURED confounding poorly controlled: max |SMD| = 1.60 after weighting.
  • Causal interpretation not supported — identification assumptions not verified.
  • Data source 'Unknown': major provenance limitation.
  • Residual covariate imbalance: age, race_concept_id, Cond: Acute myocardial infarction, Cond: Congestive rheumatic heart failure, Cond: Atherosclerosis of arteries of the extremities, Cond: Hypertensive disorder, Cond: Cerebral artery occlusion, Cond: Carotid artery stenosis, Cond: Chronic kidney disease stage 4, Cond: Left ventricular hypertrophy, Cond: Microalbuminuria, Cond: Left ventricular diastolic dysfunction, Proc: Arterial bypass graft, Proc: Fluoroscopy guided percutaneous transluminal angioplasty of carotid artery with contrast, Proc: Angiectomy with anastomosis of lower limb artery.

8. Interpretation & Next Steps

  • Operational feasibility: Yes
  • Effect estimation reliability: Poor
  • Clinical interpretability: Not supported
  • Causal interpretability: Not supported

Recommend next analyses: longer follow-up, sensitivity analyses, improved confounding control.

Final statement: This analysis is exploratory and assesses pipeline feasibility. It is not causal evidence or a clinical recommendation.

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria: Inclusion Criteria: - Type 2 diabetes - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease - HbA1c: 7.0% or above - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s) Exclusion Criteria: - Type 1 diabetes - Use of a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist (exenatide, liraglutide or other) or pramlintide or any dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitor within the 3 months prior to screening (trial start) - Use of insulin other than human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin within 3 months prior to screening. Short-term use of other insulin during this period in connection with intercurrent illness is allowed, at Investigator's discretion
trialMetadata.enrichedCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
  - >50% stenosis of coronary, carotid, or lower extremity arteries
  - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease
  - Ankle-brachial index <0.9
  - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Anti-diabetic drug naïve or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Asymptomatic cardiac ischemia documented by positive nuclear imaging test, exercise test or dobutamine stress echo
  - Chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III
  - Chronic renal failure:
  - Glycated hemoglobin ≥7.0%
  - HbA1c: 7.0% or above
  - History of symptomatic CHD documented by positive exercise stress test or any cardiac imaging or unstable angina with ECG changes
  - Hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG or imaging
  - Left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction by imaging
  - Microalbuminuria or proteinuria
  - No Prior cardiovascular disease group: Age ≥60 y and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior MI
  - Prior cardiovascular disease cohort: age ≥50 and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior coronary, carotid or peripheral arterial revascularization
  - Prior stroke or TIA
  - Type 2 diabetes
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - Acute coronary or cerebrovascular event in the previous 14 days
  - Acute decompensation of glycemic control
  - Calcitonin ≥50 ng/L
  - Chronic heart failure (NYHA class IV)

Inclusion Criteria:

* Male or female 18 years or older who has been hospitalised for chest pain and potential ACS
* Females of child-bearing potential must have a negative pregnancy test at enrollment and be willing to use 2 methods of reliable contraception

Exclusion Criteria:

* Persons with moderate or severe liver disease
* Persons who have already been treated with an invasive (angioplasty) procedure for the current episode of ACS
* Persons who are being treated with blood clotting agents that cannot be stopped

A Comparison of Ticagrelor (AZD6140) and Clopidogrel in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome

1. Clinical Question

Population: Patients with non-ST or ST elevation acute coronary syndromes (ACS).

Intervention: Ticagrelor initiation.

Comparator: Non-treated ticagrelor (Non-initiation of ticagrelor among eligible patients).

Outcome: Death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke.

Estimand: Intention-to-treat (ITT) analogue.

Emulation Scope: Short-horizon emulation, not full replication.

2. Target Trial Specification

Component Original Trial Emulation Mismatch Risk
Eligibility Hospitalized for chest pain and potential ACS, age ≥18 Patients with ACS, age ≥18 Moderate
Treatment strategy Ticagrelor initiation Initiation of ticagrelor at index date Moderate
Comparator strategy Clopidogrel Non-initiation of ticagrelor among eligible patients (target minus treated) High
Time zero Randomization date Date of first eligible ticagrelor prescription for treated patients; corresponding index date assignment for comparator patients Moderate
Outcome Death from vascular causes, myocardial infarction, stroke Primary Outcome Moderate
Follow-up 365 days 30 days High
Causal contrast Ticagrelor vs. Clopidogrel Ticagrelor vs. Non-treated ticagrelor High
Confounding control Randomization IPTW (PSM fallback) High

3. Data Source & Cohort Construction

Data provenance: Unknown (major limitation).

Cohort sizes: Treatment N = 191, Comparator N = 918.

Treatment definition: Initiation of ticagrelor at index date.

Comparator definition: Non-initiation of ticagrelor among eligible patients.

Eligibility criteria summary: Patients with ACS, age ≥18.

Time parameters: Washout period = 180 days, Grace period = 30 days, Follow-up duration = 30 days.

4. Confounding Control & Diagnostics

Analysis method: IPTW was used.

Balance diagnostics: 9 covariates were checked.

Max |SMD| after weighting: 1.3582.

Propensity score weighting did NOT achieve adequate covariate balance. The reported effect estimate is highly vulnerable to residual confounding.

Imbalanced covariates (|SMD| > 0.1): Age, Cond: Coronary arteriosclerosis, Cond: Peripheral vascular disease, Cond: Myocardial infarction.

Limitations: Measured confounders controlled, but unmeasured confounding remains.

5. Results

Total outcome events: 149 (treatment: 18, comparator: 131).

Hazard Ratio: 0.7503, 95% CI: 0.5523-1.0195, p-value: 0.0663.

Statistical significance: Not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.05). Estimate is imprecise.

6. Comparison with Original Trial

  • Follow-up duration: Original: 365 days, Emulation: 30 days.
  • Enrollment: Original: 18,624, Emulation: 1,109.
  • Outcome events: Not specified for original.
  • Hazard Ratio: Not specified for original.

This emulation differs materially from the original trial in follow-up duration, enrollment size, and treatment definition. Concordance assessment must be qualified by the mismatch analysis.

7. Limitations

  • Short follow-up (30 days < 365 days).
  • Unmeasured confounding (IPTW/PSM controls only measured confounders).
  • MEASURED confounding poorly controlled: max |SMD| = 1.36 after weighting.
  • Causal interpretation not supported — identification assumptions not verified.
  • Data source 'Unknown': major provenance limitation.
  • Residual covariate imbalance: age, Cond: Coronary arteriosclerosis, Cond: Peripheral vascular disease, Cond: Myocardial infarction.

8. Interpretation & Next Steps

  • Operational feasibility: Yes
  • Effect estimation reliability: Poor
  • Clinical interpretability: Not supported
  • Causal interpretability: Not supported

Recommend next analyses: longer follow-up, sensitivity analyses, and addressing data source limitations.

Time zero Randomization date Date of first eligible ticagrelor prescription for treated patients; corresponding index date assignment for comparator patients Moderate

Confounding control Randomization IPTW (PSM fallback) High

3. Data Source & Cohort Construction

Data provenance: Unknown (major limitation).

Cohort sizes: Treatment N = 191, Comparator N = 918.

Treatment definition: Initiation of ticagrelor at index date.

Comparator definition: Non-initiation of ticagrelor among eligible patients.

Eligibility criteria summary: Patients with ACS, age ≥18.

Time parameters: Washout period = 180 days, Grace period = 30 days, Follow-up duration = 30 days.

4. Confounding Control & Diagnostics

Analysis method: IPTW was used.

Balance diagnostics: 9 covariates were checked.

Max |SMD| after weighting: 1.3582.

Propensity score weighting did NOT achieve adequate covariate balance. The reported effect estimate is highly vulnerable to residual confounding.

Imbalanced covariates (|SMD| > 0.1): Age, Cond: Coronary arteriosclerosis, Cond: Peripheral vascular disease, Cond: Myocardial infarction.

Limitations: Measured confounders controlled, but unmeasured confounding remains.

5. Results

Total outcome events: 149 (treatment: 18, comparator: 131).

Hazard Ratio: 0.7503, 95% CI: 0.5523-1.0195, p-value: 0.0663.

Statistical significance: Not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.05). Estimate is imprecise.

6. Comparison with Original Trial

  • Follow-up duration: Original: 365 days, Emulation: 30 days.
  • Enrollment: Original: 18,624, Emulation: 1,109.
  • Outcome events: Not specified for original.
  • Hazard Ratio: Not specified for original.

This emulation differs materially from the original trial in follow-up duration, enrollment size, and treatment definition. Concordance assessment must be qualified by the mismatch analysis.

7. Limitations

  • Short follow-up (30 days < 365 days).
  • Unmeasured confounding (IPTW/PSM controls only measured confounders).
  • MEASURED confounding poorly controlled: max |SMD| = 1.36 after weighting.
  • Causal interpretation not supported — identification assumptions not verified.
  • Data source 'Unknown': major provenance limitation.
  • Residual covariate imbalance: age, Cond: Coronary arteriosclerosis, Cond: Peripheral vascular disease, Cond: Myocardial infarction.

8. Interpretation & Next Steps

  • Operational feasibility: Yes
  • Effect estimation reliability: Poor
  • Clinical interpretability: Not supported
  • Causal interpretability: Not supported

Recommend next analyses: longer follow-up, sensitivity analyses, and improved confounding control.

This analysis is a pipeline feasibility and exploratory study and is NOT causal evidence or a clinical recommendation.

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus prior to informed consent
2. Male or female patients on diet and exercise regimen who are drug naive or pre treated with any background therapy. Antidiabetic therapy has to be unchanged for 12 weeks prior to randomization.
3. Glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) of \>= 7.0% and \<=10% for patients on background therapy or HbA1c \>= 7.0% and \<= 9.0% for drug naive patients
4. Age \>= 18 years
5. Body Mass index \<= 45 at Visit 1
6. Signed and dated informed consent
7. High cardiovascular risk

Exclusion criteria:

1. Uncontrolled hyperglycaemia with a glucose level \>240 mg/dl (\>13.3 mmol/L) after an overnight fast during placebo run-in and confirmed by a second measurement (not on the same day)
2. Indication of liver disease, defined by serum levels of either alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase ALT or alkaline phosphatase above 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN) as determined at screening and/or run in.
3. Planned cardiac surgery or angioplasty within 3 months
4. Impaired renal function, defined as Glomerular Filtration Rate \<30 ml/min (severe renal impairment, Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula) during screening or run in.
5. Bariatric surgery within the past two years and other gastrointestinal surgeries that induce chronic malabsorption
6. Blood dyscrasias or any disorders causing haemolysis or unstable Red Blood Cell (e.g. malaria, babesiosis, haemolytic anemia)
7. Medical history of cancer (except for basal cell carcinoma) and/or treatment for cancer within the last 5 years
8. Contraindications to background therapy according to the local label
9. Treatment with anti-obesity drugs (e.g. sibutramine, orlistat) 3 months prior to informed consent or any other treatment at the time of screening (i.e. surgery, aggressive diet regimen, etc.) leading to unstable body weight
10. Current treatment with systemic steroids at time of informed consent or change in dosage of thyroid hormones within 6 weeks prior to informed consent or any other uncontrolled endocrine disorder except type 2 diabetes mellitus
11. Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation \<+ 1 year prior to informed consent) who:

    * are nursing or pregnant or
    * are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control, or do not plan to continue using this method throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial. Acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems, oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence, double barrier method and vasectomised partner
12. Alcohol or drug abuse within the 3 months prior to informed consent that would interfere with trial participation or any ongoing condition leading to a decreased compliance to study procedures or study drug intake
13. Participation in another trial with an investigational drug within 30 days prior to informed consent
14. Any other clinical condition that would jeopardize patients safety while participating in this clinical trial
15. Acute coronary syndrome, stroke or TIA within 2 months prior to informed consent

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Documented diagnosis of T2DM before visit 1(screening).
2. Male or female patients who are drug-naïve or pre-treated with any antidiabetic background medication, excluding treatment with Glucagon-like Peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, Dipeptidyl-peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitors or Sodium Glucose Linked Transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors if =\> consecutive 7 days.
3. Stable antidiabetic background medication (unchanged daily dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to randomization. If insulin is part of the background therapy, the average daily insulin dose should not have changed by more than 10% within the 8 weeks prior to randomization compared with the daily insulin dose at randomization.
4. HbA1c of =\> 6.5% and \<= 10.0% at Visit 1 (screening)
5. Age =\> 18 years at Visit 1(screening). For Japan only: Age =\> 20 years at Visit 1
6. Body Mass Index (BMI) \<= 45 kg/m2 at Visit 1 (screening)
7. Signed and dated written informed consent by date of Visit 1(screening) in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation prior to any study related procedure
8. High risk of cardiovascular (CV) events defined by: 1) albuminuria (micro or macro) and previous macrovascular disease and/or 2) impaired renal function with predefined Urine Albumin Creatinine Ratio (UACR)

Exclusion criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Treatment (=\> 7 consecutive days) with GLP-1 receptor agonists, other DPP-4 inhibitors or SGLT-2 inhibitors prior to informed consent. Note: This also includes clinical trials where these antidiabetic drugs have been provided to the patient.
3. Active liver disease or impaired hepatic function, defined by serum levels of either Alanine Transaminase (ALT) (SGPT), Aspartate transaminase (AST) (SGOT), or alkaline phosphatase (AP) =\> 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN) as determined at Visit 1.
4. Estimated Glomerular filtration Rate (eGFR) \<15 ml/min/1.73 m2 (severe renal impairment or End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) formula), as determined during screening at Visit 1 and/or the need for maintenance dialysis.
5. Any previous (or planned within next 12 months) bariatric surgery (open or laparoscopic) or intervention (gastric sleeve).
6. Pre-planned coronary artery re-vascularisation (PCI, CABG) or any previous PCI and/or CABG \<= 2 months prior informed consent.
7. Known hypersensitivity or allergy to the investigational products or its excipients.
8. Any previous or current alcohol or drug abuse that would interfere with trial participation in the opinion of the investigator.
9. Participation in another trial with an investigational drug ongoing or within 2 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
10. Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation = 1 year prior to informed consent) who are nursing or pregnant, are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control (acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems (IUDs/IUSs), oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence (if allowed by local authorities), double barrier method and vasectomised partner) or do not plan to continue using acceptable method of birth control throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial.
11. Patients considered unreliable by the investigator concerning the requirements for follow up during the study and/or compliance with study drug administration, have a life expectancy less than 5 years for non-CV causes, or have cancer other than non-melanoma skin cancer within last 3 years, or has any other condition than mentioned which in the opinion of the investigator, would not allow safe participation in the study.
12. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS), diagnosed \<= 2 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
13. Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) \<= 3 months prior to visit 1 (screening).

  - Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation = 1 year prior to informed consent) who are nursing or pregnant, are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control (acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems (IUDs/IUSs), oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence (if allowed by local authorities), double barrier method and vasectomised partner) or do not plan to continue using acceptable method of birth control throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial.
  - Pre-planned coronary artery re-vascularisation (PCI, CABG) or any previous PCI and/or CABG <= 2 months prior informed consent.
  - Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) <= 3 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
  - Treatment (=> 7 consecutive days) with GLP-1 receptor agonists, other DPP-4 inhibitors or SGLT-2 inhibitors prior to informed consent. Note: This also includes clinical trials where these antidiabetic drugs have been provided to the patient.
  - Type 1 diabetes mellitus.

trialMetadata.officialTitle: A Multicentre, International, Randomised, Parallel Group, Double Blind Study to Evaluate Cardiovascular Safety of Linagliptin Versus Glimepiride in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus at High Cardiovascular Risk.
trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Type 2 diabetes
2. Elevated glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c): 6.5 - 8.5%, inclusive, if treatment naïve or mono-/dual therapy with metformin and/or an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor; 6.5 - 7.5%, inclusive, if treatment with sulphonylurea/glinide in mono- or dual (with metformin OR an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) therapy)
3. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease OR specified diabetes end-organ damage OR age =\> 70 years OR two or more specified cardiovascular risk factor
4. BMI =\< 45kg/m²
5. age between \>= 40 and =\< 85 years
6. signed and dated written International Conference of Harmonisation( ICF)
7. stable anti-diabetic background for at least 8 wks before study start

Exclusion criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes
2. Treatment with other antidiabetic drugs (e.g. rosiglitazone, pioglitazone, Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) analogue/agonists, Dipeptidyl-peptidase IV (DPP-IV) inhibitors or any insulin) prior to informed consent (previous short term use of insulin (up to two weeks) is allowed if taken at least 8 weeks prior informed consent)
3. treatment with any anti-obesity drug less than 3 months before ICF
4. uncontrolled hyperglycemia
5. previous or planned bariatric surgery or intervention
6. current or planned system corticoid treatment
7. change in thyroid hormones treatment
8. acute liver disease or impaired hepatic function
9. pre-planned coronary artery revascularization within 6 months of ICF
10. known hypersensitivity to any of the components
11. Inappropriateness of glimepiride treatment for renal safety issues according to local prescribing information
12. congestive heart failure class III or IV
13. acute or chronic metabolic acidosis
14. hereditary galactose intolerance
15. alcohol or drug abuse
16. participation in another trail with IMP given 2 months before Investigational Medicinal/Medical Product (IMP) start
17. pre-menopausal women who are nursing or pregnant or of child-bearing potential and not willing to use acceptable method of birth control
18. patients considered reliable by the investigator
19. acute coronary syndrome =\< 6 wks before ICF
20. stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) =\< 3 months prior to ICF

trialMetadata.officialTitle: A Phase 3, Active (Warfarin) Controlled, Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel Arm Study to Evaluate Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban in Preventing Stroke and Systemic Embolism in Subjects With Nonvalvular Atrial Fibrillation
trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Males and females ≥ 18 yrs with atrial fibrillation (AF) and one or more of the following risk factors for stroke:
* Age ≥ 75, previous stroke
* transient ischemic attack (TIA) or Systemic Embolism (SE)
* Symptomatic congestive heart failure or left ventricular dysfunction with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 40%
* Diabetes mellitus or hypertension requiring pharmacological treatment
trialMetadata.enrichedCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
  - * Males and females ≥ 18 yrs with atrial fibrillation (AF) and one or more of the following risk factors for stroke:
  - Age 75 years or older
  - Age ≥ 18 years
  - Age ≥ 75, previous stroke
  - Diabetes mellitus
  - Diabetes mellitus or hypertension requiring pharmacological treatment
  - ECG at the time of enrollment
  - Either symptomatic congestive heart failure within 3 months or left ventricular dysfunction with an LV ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 40% by echocardiography, radionuclide study or contrast angiography
  - For entry into the study, the following criteria MUST be met
  - Holter recording, or intracardiac electrogram (from an implanted pacemaker or defibrillator)
  - If not in atrial fibrillation/flutter at the time of enrollment, must have atrial fibrillation/flutter documented on two separate occasions, not due to a reversible cause at least 2 weeks apart in the 12 months prior to enrollment. Atrial fibrillation/flutter may be documented by ECG, or as an episode lasting at least one minute on a rhythm strip,
  - In atrial fibrillation or atrial flutter not due to a reversible cause and documented by
  - One or more of the following risk factor(s) for stroke:
  - Prior stroke, TIA or systemic embolus
  - Symptomatic congestive heart failure or left ventricular dysfunction with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) ≤ 40%
  - Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) must be using an adequate method of contraception to avoid pregnancy throughout the
  - transient ischemic attack (TIA) or Systemic Embolism (SE)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - (e.g. previous intracranial hemorrhage)
  - > 100 mm Hg)
  - ALT or AST > 2X ULN or a Total Bilirubin ≥ 1.5X ULN (unless an alternative causative factor [e.g., Gilbert’s syndrome] is identified)
  - Active alcohol or drug abuse, or psychosocial reasons that make study participation impractical
  - Active infective endocarditis
  - Atrial fibrillation or flutter due to reversible causes (e.g. thyrotoxicosis, pericarditis)
  - Clinically significant (moderate or severe) mitral stenosis
  - Conditions other than atrial fibrillation that require chronic anticoagulation (e.g
  - Hemoglobin < 9 g/dL
  - Inability to comply with INR monitoring
  - Increased bleeding risk that is believed to be a contraindication to oral anticoagulation
  - Persistent, uncontrolled hypertension (systolic BP > 180 mm Hg, or diastolic BP
  - Planned atrial fibrillation or flutter ablation procedure
  - Planned major surgery
  - Platelet count ≤ 100,000/ mm
  - Prior
  - Recent ischemic stroke (within 7 days)
  - Required treatment with aspirin > 165 mg/day
  - Severe comorbid condition with life expectancy of ≤ 1 year
  - Severe renal insufficiency (serum creatinine > 2.5 mg/dL or a calculated creatinine clearance < 25 mL/min, See Section 6.3.2.2)
  - Simultaneous treatment with both aspirin and a thienopyridine (e.g., clopidogrel, ticlopidine)
  - Use of an unapproved, investigational drug or device within the past 30 days
  - prosthetic mechanical heart valve)

trialMetadata.briefTitle: CAROLINA: Cardiovascular Outcome Study of Linagliptin Versus Glimepiride in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
trialMetadata.officialTitle: A Multicentre, International, Randomised, Parallel Group, Double Blind Study to Evaluate Cardiovascular Safety of Linagliptin Versus Glimepiride in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus at High Cardiovascular Risk.
trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Type 2 diabetes
2. Elevated glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c): 6.5 - 8.5%, inclusive, if treatment naïve or mono-/dual therapy with metformin and/or an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor; 6.5 - 7.5%, inclusive, if treatment with sulphonylurea/glinide in mono- or dual (with metformin OR an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) therapy)
3. Pre-existing cardiovascular disease OR specified diabetes end-organ damage OR age =\> 70 years OR two or more specified cardiovascular risk factor
4. BMI =\< 45kg/m²
5. age between \>= 40 and =\< 85 years
6. signed and dated written International Conference of Harmonisation( ICF)
7. stable anti-diabetic background for at least 8 wks before study start

Exclusion criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes
2. Treatment with other antidiabetic drugs (e.g. rosiglitazone, pioglitazone, Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) analogue/agonists, Dipeptidyl-peptidase IV (DPP-IV) inhibitors or any insulin) prior to informed consent (previous short term use of insulin (up to two weeks) is allowed if taken at least 8 weeks prior informed consent)
3. treatment with any anti-obesity drug less than 3 months before ICF
4. uncontrolled hyperglycemia
5. previous or planned bariatric surgery or intervention
6. current or planned system corticoid treatment
7. change in thyroid hormones treatment
8. acute liver disease or impaired hepatic function
9. pre-planned coronary artery revascularization within 6 months of ICF
10. known hypersensitivity to any of the components
11. Inappropriateness of glimepiride treatment for renal safety issues according to local prescribing information
12. congestive heart failure class III or IV
13. acute or chronic metabolic acidosis
14. hereditary galactose intolerance
15. alcohol or drug abuse
16. participation in another trail with IMP given 2 months before Investigational Medicinal/Medical Product (IMP) start
17. pre-menopausal women who are nursing or pregnant or of child-bearing potential and not willing to use acceptable method of birth control
18. patients considered reliable by the investigator
19. acute coronary syndrome =\< 6 wks before ICF
20. stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) =\< 3 months prior to ICF

trialMetadata.officialTitle: A Phase III, Multicentre, International, Randomised, Parallel Group, Double Blind Cardiovascular Safety Study of BI 10773 (10 mg and 25 mg Administered Orally Once Daily) Compared to Usual Care in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Patients With Increased Cardiovascular Risk
trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus prior to informed consent
2. Male or female patients on diet and exercise regimen who are drug naive or pre treated with any background therapy. Antidiabetic therapy has to be unchanged for 12 weeks prior to randomization.
3. Glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c) of \>= 7.0% and \<=10% for patients on background therapy or HbA1c \>= 7.0% and \<= 9.0% for drug naive patients
4. Age \>= 18 years
5. Body Mass index \<= 45 at Visit 1
6. Signed and dated informed consent
7. High cardiovascular risk

Exclusion criteria:

1. Uncontrolled hyperglycaemia with a glucose level \>240 mg/dl (\>13.3 mmol/L) after an overnight fast during placebo run-in and confirmed by a second measurement (not on the same day)
2. Indication of liver disease, defined by serum levels of either alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase ALT or alkaline phosphatase above 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN) as determined at screening and/or run in.
3. Planned cardiac surgery or angioplasty within 3 months
4. Impaired renal function, defined as Glomerular Filtration Rate \<30 ml/min (severe renal impairment, Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula) during screening or run in.
5. Bariatric surgery within the past two years and other gastrointestinal surgeries that induce chronic malabsorption
6. Blood dyscrasias or any disorders causing haemolysis or unstable Red Blood Cell (e.g. malaria, babesiosis, haemolytic anemia)
7. Medical history of cancer (except for basal cell carcinoma) and/or treatment for cancer within the last 5 years
8. Contraindications to background therapy according to the local label
9. Treatment with anti-obesity drugs (e.g. sibutramine, orlistat) 3 months prior to informed consent or any other treatment at the time of screening (i.e. surgery, aggressive diet regimen, etc.) leading to unstable body weight
10. Current treatment with systemic steroids at time of informed consent or change in dosage of thyroid hormones within 6 weeks prior to informed consent or any other uncontrolled endocrine disorder except type 2 diabetes mellitus
11. Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation \<+ 1 year prior to informed consent) who:

    * are nursing or pregnant or
    * are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control, or do not plan to continue using this method throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial. Acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems, oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence, double barrier method and vasectomised partner
12. Alcohol or drug abuse within the 3 months prior to informed consent that would interfere with trial participation or any ongoing condition leading to a decreased compliance to study procedures or study drug intake
13. Participation in another trial with an investigational drug within 30 days prior to informed consent
14. Any other clinical condition that would jeopardize patients safety while participating in this clinical trial
15. Acute coronary syndrome, stroke or TIA within 2 months prior to informed consent

trialMetadata.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion criteria:

1. Documented diagnosis of T2DM before visit 1(screening).
2. Male or female patients who are drug-naïve or pre-treated with any antidiabetic background medication, excluding treatment with Glucagon-like Peptide 1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, Dipeptidyl-peptidase 4 (DPP-4) inhibitors or Sodium Glucose Linked Transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors if =\> consecutive 7 days.
3. Stable antidiabetic background medication (unchanged daily dose) for at least 8 weeks prior to randomization. If insulin is part of the background therapy, the average daily insulin dose should not have changed by more than 10% within the 8 weeks prior to randomization compared with the daily insulin dose at randomization.
4. HbA1c of =\> 6.5% and \<= 10.0% at Visit 1 (screening)
5. Age =\> 18 years at Visit 1(screening). For Japan only: Age =\> 20 years at Visit 1
6. Body Mass Index (BMI) \<= 45 kg/m2 at Visit 1 (screening)
7. Signed and dated written informed consent by date of Visit 1(screening) in accordance with Good Clinical Practice (GCP) and local legislation prior to any study related procedure
8. High risk of cardiovascular (CV) events defined by: 1) albuminuria (micro or macro) and previous macrovascular disease and/or 2) impaired renal function with predefined Urine Albumin Creatinine Ratio (UACR)

Exclusion criteria:

1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Treatment (=\> 7 consecutive days) with GLP-1 receptor agonists, other DPP-4 inhibitors or SGLT-2 inhibitors prior to informed consent. Note: This also includes clinical trials where these antidiabetic drugs have been provided to the patient.
3. Active liver disease or impaired hepatic function, defined by serum levels of either Alanine Transaminase (ALT) (SGPT), Aspartate transaminase (AST) (SGOT), or alkaline phosphatase (AP) =\> 3 x upper limit of normal (ULN) as determined at Visit 1.
4. Estimated Glomerular filtration Rate (eGFR) \<15 ml/min/1.73 m2 (severe renal impairment or End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD), Modification of Diet in Renal Disease (MDRD) formula), as determined during screening at Visit 1 and/or the need for maintenance dialysis.
5. Any previous (or planned within next 12 months) bariatric surgery (open or laparoscopic) or intervention (gastric sleeve).
6. Pre-planned coronary artery re-vascularisation (PCI, CABG) or any previous PCI and/or CABG \<= 2 months prior informed consent.
7. Known hypersensitivity or allergy to the investigational products or its excipients.
8. Any previous or current alcohol or drug abuse that would interfere with trial participation in the opinion of the investigator.
9. Participation in another trial with an investigational drug ongoing or within 2 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
10. Pre-menopausal women (last menstruation = 1 year prior to informed consent) who are nursing or pregnant, are of child-bearing potential and are not practicing an acceptable method of birth control (acceptable methods of birth control include tubal ligation, transdermal patch, intra uterine devices/systems (IUDs/IUSs), oral, implantable or injectable contraceptives, sexual abstinence (if allowed by local authorities), double barrier method and vasectomised partner) or do not plan to continue using acceptable method of birth control throughout the study and do not agree to submit to periodic pregnancy testing during participation in the trial.
11. Patients considered unreliable by the investigator concerning the requirements for follow up during the study and/or compliance with study drug administration, have a life expectancy less than 5 years for non-CV causes, or have cancer other than non-melanoma skin cancer within last 3 years, or has any other condition than mentioned which in the opinion of the investigator, would not allow safe participation in the study.
12. Acute coronary syndrome (ACS), diagnosed \<= 2 months prior to visit 1 (screening).
13. Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA) \<= 3 months prior to visit 1 (screening).

trialMetadata.enrichedCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:
  - >50% stenosis of coronary, carotid, or lower extremity arteries
  - Age min. 50 years at screening and concomitant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease or chronic renal failure or chronic heart failure OR age min. 60 years at screening and other specified risk factors of cardiovascular disease
  - Ankle-brachial index <0.9
  - Anti-diabetic drug naive or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs (OADs) or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Anti-diabetic drug naïve or treated with one or more oral anti-diabetic drugs or treated with human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin, alone or in combination with OAD(s)
  - Asymptomatic cardiac ischemia documented by positive nuclear imaging test, exercise test or dobutamine stress echo
  - Chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III
  - Chronic renal failure:
  - Glycated hemoglobin ≥7.0%
  - HbA1c: 7.0% or above
  - History of symptomatic CHD documented by positive exercise stress test or any cardiac imaging or unstable angina with ECG changes
  - Hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy by ECG or imaging
  - Left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction by imaging
  - Microalbuminuria or proteinuria
  - No Prior cardiovascular disease group: Age ≥60 y and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior MI
  - Prior cardiovascular disease cohort: age ≥50 and ≥1 of the following criteria:
  - Prior coronary, carotid or peripheral arterial revascularization
  - Prior stroke or TIA
  - Type 2 diabetes
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault formula)
  -  eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2 (Modification of Diet in Renal Disease formula)

Exclusion Criteria:
  - Acute coronary or cerebrovascular event in the previous 14 days
  - Acute decompensation of glycemic control
  - Calcitonin ≥50 ng/L
  - Chronic heart failure (NYHA class IV)
  - Current continuous renal replacement therapy
  - Currently planned coronary, carotid, or peripheral artery revascularization
  - End-stage liver disease
  - Family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - History of solid organ transplant or awaiting solid organ transplant
  - Malignant neoplasm
  - Personal history of non-familial medullary thyroid carcinoma
  - Type 1 diabetes
  - Use of a GLP-1 receptor agonist (exenatide, liraglutide or other) or pramlintide or any DPP-4 inhibitor within the 3 months prior to screening
  - Use of insulin other than human NPH insulin or long-acting insulin analogue or premixed insulin within 3 months prior to screening. Short-term use of other insulin during this period in connection with intercurrent illness is allowed, at Investigator’s discretion
